page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture utilizing an Intel Xeon 8163 processor. The configuration provides 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, offering a dedicated CPU allocation. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz and includes a 33 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by lower-tier results in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, alongside poor single-threaded compression and decompression speeds. However, the 16-vCPU dedicated allocation allows the instance to achieve average multi-core performance. Multi-threaded benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression, consistently fall within the middle tier. Memory bandwidth and database operations also demonstrate average performance characteristics, with Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput maintaining stable, mid-range metrics.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.n2.3xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without the premium cost of high-frequency or specialized compute hardware. The lack of local storage means workloads must rely on network-attached storage options. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads that benefit from multi-threaded execution but do not demand extreme single-core performance. Appropriate use cases include mid-sized web serving, multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
